news.title: Michael Saylor hints at first bitcoin purchase in two months as bitcoin nears $79,000
news.summary: Bitcoin rebounds from Friday’s low as Strategy’s valuation expands and bitcoin dominance climbs above 60%.

news.title: From Hawala to Swift: Inside the 1,000-year battle to move money safely
news.summary: Finance has spent centuries decoupling wealth from physical transport, but constantly erasing friction creates vectors for increasingly high-tech exploits.

news.title: Crypto market makers are cashing in on bitcoin's rally - without betting on direction
news.summary: As bitcoin surges back above $80,000, sophisticated trading firms are quietly collecting yield rather than making directional bet.

news.title: A $1.1 million crypto card hack crashed a neobank's token 49%
news.summary: The exploit caused the neobank's AVICI token to drop 49% from a 24-hour high, hitting a record low before paring some of the losses.

news.title: Ditching 'digital gold': BPI study suggests everyday Americans prefer control and micro-investing
news.summary: A new survey suggests some of bitcoin's most familiar sales pitches of changing the world may be poorly suited to a majority of prospective buyers.

news.title: Inside the high-stakes battle between digital dollars and Swift's massive money engine
news.summary: Crypto executives say new blockchain payment infrastructure could make Swift obsolete. Bankers say its 11,500-institution network gives it the power to absorb the technology instead.

news.title: The next trillion-dollar currency may not be a stablecoin — it might not even have a name yet
news.summary: AI agents are coming. They will need to pay each other. Crypto executives agree on the problem but disagree sharply on the solution, and one thinks the answer has not been invented yet.

news.title: Tokenized assets are busier than the data shows
news.summary: When you strip out what was never mobile, correct for who's holding what and why, add back what works off-contract, the utilization of tokenized assets looks close to 20%, argues Katana’s Matthew Fisher.

news.title: ‘I feel shoehorned’: My father funded my $800,000 Roth IRA. Does that give him the right to say how I invest it?
news.summary: “His argument is essentially that, since my parents provided the money for the Roth, they have a say in how I invest it.”

news.title: My mother, 91, has dementia. Every bank says I need her signature to unlock her $100,000 stock certificate. What can I do?
news.summary: “These shares are the only assets in her estate without designated beneficiaries.”

news.title: My contractor handed my $42,000 pool upgrade to a subcontractor I had already rejected. What can I do?
news.summary: “I specifically rejected Contractor A because of his reputation.”

news.title: Does a 2% beneficiary inherit 100% if the 98% beneficiary dies in a car accident? Asking for a friend.
news.summary: “I’m curious what would happen if the account owner were to die suddenly at the same time as the 98% beneficiary.”

news.title: Am I too old for Roth conversions? I’m 84 and my wife is 77. We have $8 million saved.
news.summary: “We are reluctant to pay a financial adviser 2% of assets — roughly $160,000 per year.”

news.title: These charts show how leverage-happy investors are transforming the stock market
news.summary: A rush of retail investors and quant funds has caused a shift toward more borrowed money and more short-term trading.

news.title: Party balloons could become a ‘luxury’ as the Iran war spurs a helium shortage
news.summary: Dollar Tree says a helium squeeze has hit sales of balloons and party supplies. Researchers note this could foreshadow higher costs for other industries that depend on the gas.
